title: free a pointer 8 bytes into an object instead of the one st_alloc returned
control: frees a; one alloc and one free in both images

asan.why: The one class where the malloc baseline is enforced by the ALLOCATOR and not only by the tool: the chunk header is not where libc expects. A bump arena ignores its argument and cannot tell a+8 from a. A free list pushes a+8 onto a size-class list and misaligns every later object in that class, so the damage appears far from here -- which is why the case records what it did instead of waiting for a crash.

valgrind.why: MEMPOOL_FREE of an address that is not a pool allocation is reported.

hwasan.why: malloc's own check. HWASan has no public custom-allocator interface, so the annotated columns are UNSUPPORTED, not MISSED (C3.4).

ubsan.why: -fsanitize=bounds needs a statically known array bound; a pointer out of an allocator has none. The row is kept so the report can say UBSan is not a heap tool rather than leaving it out.

lowfat.why: LowFat can check that a freed pointer is its region's base, which is a bounds question; to verify.

status: written, smoke-run on malloc and arena; server run pending (A5)
